texts: mixed: the scattering, the agent, the date, the evening and the location around the Lantern are all right, but 'fresh' and 'ground' are predicated of the feather group as a single object rather than of each feather, which our plural rules bar. Any descriptive adjective sitting on a plural noun has to take that per-member route, so the wording that gets it right every time states it as an explicit universal: 'On day 495 of Year 2, Bevin Coombe scattered feathers around the Stilllight Lantern in the evening. Each of the feathers was fresh and ground.'
good. a burn event on the named Lantern with a genuine manner adverb, and 'that night' correctly picks up day 495's terms.
good. the seeing, the pale shape and the water of the Sunken Cove all land, with 'near the water' attached to the shape.

bad: the 'before' clause is parsed as an event that actually happened — the parse asserts at full strength that the shape reached the Stilllight Lantern, the opposite of what you wrote — and we have no way to order an event against one that never occurred. State the non-occurrence directly instead of ordering against it: 'The shape turned away, and the shape never reached the Stilllight Lantern.'
good. a report event with agent, the earlier seeing as what was reported, and the Council as recipient.

mixed: the session, the Council, the afternoon and the ordering after the report are all recorded, but the 'next' — that it was the following day — is dropped, because the reporting sentence carries no date for it to count from. Date the session outright: 'The Council held an emergency session in the afternoon of day 496 of Year 2.' (Putting a date on the reporting sentence instead would fix it just as well.)

bad: 'logged X as Y' has no licensed form for us and the hedge 'possible' has nowhere to sit, so the parse asserted outright that the report IS a wraith near-miss — a stronger claim than you made — while the compliant alternative is to drop the classification and lose it entirely. Put the classification in a finite clause with the hedge as a modal: 'The Council logged the report, and judged that the report might be a wraith near-miss.'
good. a keep event with the doubled feather ration, the Stilllight Station as location and the two months as a duration measure.

mixed: the order, its addressees and the alert state all land, but 'stay' — the keep-on-being-alert part — leaves no trace, and our rules do not settle how a continuation state rides inside an order given to a group. If that nuance matters, make the prior state its own clause: 'The keepers of the West Row were alert, and the Council told them to stay alert.'

mixed: the non-occurrence is correctly recorded at strength 0 with 'further' on the sighting, but it carries no past marker, so a past-tense question about a later sighting may not match it. An explicit past copula makes the tense unmissable: 'There was no further sighting.'
good. the judgment is sealed, so the prevention is recorded as the Council's view rather than asserted as fact, with the feather warding typed and given its genus.
